page: Vultr vbm-32c-755gb-amd is a bare metal server powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9354P processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration features 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs operating at a base clock speed of 3.25 GHz. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing 12.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 960 GB SSD, and the system includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across several critical vectors. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng ranks in the top 10%, while multi-core performance is positioned in the top 25%. The DDR5 memory subsystem delivers top-tier read and write bandwidth for large uncached blocks, alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score. Database operations and LLM inference tasks, specifically text generation using a medium 7B model, also achieve top-tier benchmark results. Static web serving throughput and Redis SET operations demonstrate strong performance in the top 25%.

From a resource density perspective, this bare metal server offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads due to its massive 768.0 GB RAM capacity and high-speed DDR5 architecture. However, a notable tradeoff is the relatively modest local storage capacity of 960 GB SSD, which may require external storage solutions for data-intensive deployments despite the server's top-tier database performance.

The Vultr vbm-32c-755gb-amd is highly suited for memory-intensive databases, large-scale Redis deployments, and memory-cached web serving. The high core count and fast memory bandwidth also make it appropriate for medium-scale LLM inference, data processing pipelines, and enterprise-grade virtualization environments that do not require hardware GPU acceleration.
